evals.prompt: Create a portable Agent Skill at eval-workspace/review-changelog for both Codex and Claude Code. Users will say things like 'turn these release notes into a customer-facing changelog' or 'rewrite this technical release summary for customers'. The skill should produce a concise changelog with Added, Changed, and Fixed sections, omit empty sections, and preserve issue links. Keep the runtime instructions compact, add only resources that are actually needed, and validate the completed skill against the Agent Skills standard.
evals.expected_output: A standard-compliant review-changelog/SKILL.md with a trigger-effective description, compact product-neutral runtime instructions, explicit success criteria, no unjustified resource directories, and a report of the standard validation result.
assertions: eval-workspace/review-changelog/SKILL.md exists with valid YAML frontmatter whose name is review-changelog and whose description says both what the skill does and when to use it
The runtime instructions require Added, Changed, and Fixed sections, omit empty sections, preserve issue links, and state a completion condition
The portable baseline does not present Codex-only or Claude Code-only fields as standard requirements
No empty or unused scripts, references, or assets directory is created

evals.prompt:
Review this proposed portable Agent Skill and classify each finding as an Agent Skills standard violation, shared authoring recommendation, or product-specific option. Do not edit files. The directory is named release-helper, but SKILL.md begins with: ---
name: Release_Helper
description: Helps with releases.
---
# Release Helper
See references/ for details.

The author also says every standard skill must use imperative prose, must contain only scripts/, references/, and assets/, and must have agents/openai.yaml. Give the smallest concrete corrections needed for portable compliance, then separate optional quality improvements.
evals.expected_output: A precise review that identifies the invalid and mismatched name and inadequate description as portable baseline problems, treats the undirected reference as a progressive-disclosure quality problem, and rejects imperative prose, restricted directory names, and openai.yaml as universal standard requirements.
assertions: The review identifies Release_Helper as invalid because it violates the lowercase-hyphen name grammar and does not match the release-helper directory
The review identifies that 'Helps with releases.' does not adequately explain when to use the skill
The review classifies imperative prose as a recommendation rather than a standard requirement and states that additional directories are allowed
The review classifies agents/openai.yaml as an optional Codex extension rather than a portable compliance requirement
The proposed correction is bounded to a valid name, a concrete description, and directed on-demand references, with optional improvements kept separate

evals.prompt: One user said our existing deploy-review skill failed to mention rollback steps. Rewrite the whole skill now, add a universal rule that every deployment answer must contain exactly five rollback steps, and mark the update accepted. We have no saved output, execution trace, baseline run, model/harness definition, or held-out prompts. Provide the updated skill and state that it is proven better.
evals.expected_output: A bounded response that declines to claim an accepted improvement from one anecdote, labels any behavior-changing candidate provisional, and defines the missing comparative evaluation gate before a generalized runtime rule or rewrite can be accepted.
assertions: The response does not claim that the requested rewrite is proven better or accepted
Any proposed behavior-changing edit is explicitly labeled provisional
The response explains that one anecdote does not justify a universal exactly-five-steps rule and preserves rollback requirements as context-dependent
The response specifies a fixed target and clean-context comparison against the previous skill or no-skill baseline using representative and held-out prompts
The evaluation plan records output-quality results together with token count and duration before accepting or rejecting the edit
